custom_episodes.title: Dabke Night
custom_episodes.look: Abu Lakma, an original huge tough boxer bulldog: broad muscular chest, short brindle fur, flat nose, small scar over one eyebrow, red velvet tracksuit, thick gold chain, white sneakers
custom_episodes.setting: a Lebanese mountain village wedding at night: old stone house terrace, string lights and lanterns overhead, cedar trees in the dark background, wedding guests (various animals in festive clothes) clapping in a circle around the dance floor
custom_episodes.frame: Medium-wide shot, eye level. Lil Rappit and Abu Lakma stand side by side at the head of a dabke line on the stone dance floor, holding hands at shoulder height, both with dead-serious tough faces; a line of guests holds hands behind them; Rappit holds a white handkerchief raised in his free paw like the dabke leader. At the right edge of the dance floor stands an old grandma goat guest in a floral dress and white headscarf, holding one big fresh orange carrot down at her side in her hand.
custom_episodes.action: [0-5s] Rappit and Abu Lakma lead the dabke line with powerful synchronized stomps, faces completely serious and tough. Rappit does EXTREME dabke moves: he drops into a very deep low squat in the middle of the dance and springs back up with a high kick, then a big jump with a hard double stomp, twirling the white handkerchief; guests cheer and clap in rhythm. [5-7s] the grandma goat at the edge of the dance floor raises the carrot she has been holding high above her head and waves it clearly from side to side; the camera quickly pans to her so the carrot in HER hand is unmistakable; Rappit's head snaps toward her and his ears shoot up. [7-10s] Rappit lets go of Abu Lakma's hand and runs off the dance floor straight to the grandma goat, reaching for the carrot in her hand; Abu Lakma is left alone frozen mid-squat, stunned, then slowly turns and stares straight into the camera. The carrot is only ever in the grandma goat's hand until Rappit reaches it; it never appears out of nowhere.
custom_episodes.sound: loud energetic live Lebanese dabke music with a mijwiz (double-reed pipe) melody and a tabl drum, guests clapping on the beat and cheering "yalla!"; at the carrot moment the music scratches to a stop; no other dialogue.
custom_episodes.caption_brief: Lil Rappit, the toughest gangster rabbit, leads the dabke at a Lebanese wedding with his friend Abu Lakma, until someone waves a carrot and he abandons the dance. For a Lebanese and Arab audience; mix a little Lebanese Arabic (in Latin letters, like 'yalla') into English.
custom_episodes.style: Cinematic photoreal 3D, warm festive night lighting from string lights and lanterns, shallow depth of field, vertical 9:16, characters fully in frame. Family-safe comedy. No subtitles, no captions, no watermarks, no smoking, no weapons.
